children: DoorDash is investing $125 million in Wonder, the parent company of its competitor Grubhub, as part of a new partnership.

The delivery company also said Tuesday it agreed to acquire Wonder's Grubhub campus dining business for $300 million, with plans to expand the service beyond college campuses to stadiums, hotels and other venues.

DoorDash's investment adds to food-hall startup Wonder's latest funding, a $650 million Series D round at a premoney valuation of $9 billion that was disclosed in July. Wonder has said it plans to use the funding to funnel further investment into automating more of its business, from cooking and delivery to menu creation.

Wonder Chief Executive Officer Marc Lore said the partnership with DoorDash will allow it to continue investing in technology, robotics and infrastructure, and help it focus on its long-term target of becoming a fully autonomous food system that can plan, make and deliver personalized meals at scale.

For DoorDash, the deal for Grubhub campus dining adds a meal-ordering service offered at more than 450 colleges and universities. The business, formerly known as Tapingo, allows students to order a meal from campus dining facilities and on-campus restaurants using its mobile app or kiosks and schedule pickup.

DoorDash said it plans to continue expanding the service in the U.S. following the close of the deal, which is expected by the first half of next year, subject to closing conditions and regulatory review.

"Adding Grubhub Campus Dining to our platform will enable us to bring greater choice and convenience to college students while streamlining operations and reducing friction for universities," DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said.
